market_context: United States/general English; cooked long-grain brown rice without special fortification
title: Brown rice: fiber, protein and nutrition

seo.title: Brown rice nutrition: calories, fiber and protein per 100 g
seo.meta_description: 100 g cooked brown rice provides ~123 kcal, 25.6 g carbs, 2.7 g protein and 1.6 g fiber, plus magnesium and manganese.
seo.search_intent: Understand the nutrition of cooked brown rice and distinguish cooked values from dry-grain values.

excerpt: Per 100 g cooked, long-grain brown rice provides about 123 kcal, 25.6 g carbohydrate, 2.7 g protein, 1.0 g fat and 1.6 g fiber. It also contains roughly 39 mg magnesium and 1.0 mg manganese. A cooked cup weighing about 202 g is around 248 kcal and 5.5 g protein.
content_html:
Brown rice keeps the bran and germ that are removed when white rice is milled. That mainly changes fiber and several micronutrients, but most of its energy still comes from carbohydrate.

Nutrition per 100 g cooked

NutrientAmount
Energy~123 kcal
Carbohydrate~25.6 g
Protein~2.74 g
Fat~0.97 g
Fiber~1.6 g
Magnesium~39 mg
Phosphorus~103 mg
Manganese~0.97 mg

These are values for cooked long-grain brown rice. Dry brown rice shows much higher numbers per 100 g because it has not yet absorbed cooking water.

A cup changes the scale

A cooked cup weighing about 202 g provides roughly 248 kcal, 51.7 g carbohydrate, 5.5 g protein and 3.2 g fiber. That serving reference is often easier to visualize than a 100 g table entry.

It is not especially high in protein

At about 2.7 g protein per 100 g cooked, brown rice provides much less protein than a similar weight of lentils, tofu, meat or fish. Its main role in a meal is usually carbohydrate and energy.

Fiber is higher than white rice, but not huge

A cooked white-rice reference has about 0.4 g fiber per 100 g versus ~1.6 g in brown rice—about four times as much. Even so, 1.6 g per 100 g is well below many cooked legumes, which can exceed 6–8 g.

Magnesium and manganese stand out

Bran and germ retain minerals. This reference provides about 39 mg magnesium and nearly 1 mg manganese per 100 g, more than many refined, unenriched white-rice entries.

Cooking method changes the final concentration

The more water rice absorbs, the less concentrated calories and nutrients become per 100 g. Two batches of cooked brown rice can therefore differ somewhat even when they started from the same dry grain.

The practical takeaway

Brown rice is mainly a carbohydrate food with somewhat more fiber and minerals than white rice. Per 100 g cooked it provides about 123 kcal and 1.6 g fiber; a cooked cup roughly doubles those amounts.

faq.question: How many calories are in cooked brown rice?
faq.answer: A USDA long-grain cooked reference provides about 123 kcal per 100 g and roughly 248 kcal per 202 g cup.

faq.question: How much fiber does brown rice have?
faq.answer: About 1.6 g per 100 g cooked, around four times the ~0.4 g in a cooked white-rice reference.

faq.question: Is brown rice high in protein?
faq.answer: Not especially. It provides about 2.7 g protein per 100 g cooked.
